title: test(cli): pin the generated `apps` i18n leaf that no provenance predicate judges
body:
Part of #16872. ⚠️ Deliberately not a closing keyword — this PR delivers the measurement, the argued shape and the tripwire, but **not** the population change that actually closes the card. Which half is left, and why it is left, is the subject of the last section.

## 1. The proposed shape: the GENERATED predicate owns a generated `apps` leaf

**`findStaleFills` owns it, and the population it walks must be derived from what the run generated rather than fixed as a section-name list.**

The argument is the module's own, already written down in `source-hash.ts`:

> - **hand-authored** — the value is a TRANSLATION, whose bytes say nothing about the source's. Stale is decided on the record alone: `recorded !== hash(currentSource)`. `findStaleLeaves`, unchanged.
> - **generated** — the value got there by being COPIED from the source (`--fill=default`). So the bytes themselves are evidence, and the record only certifies WHICH source revision they are a copy of.

So the discriminator the module commits to is **how the leaf got there**, not which section name it sits under. `GENERATED_SECTIONS` / `HAND_AUTHORED_SECTIONS` are a *proxy* for that, and the proxy is exact only while `--objects-only` is the only emission mode. Under `--no-objects-only --fill=default` an `apps` leaf is a source copy by construction, so the proxy misclassifies it — and misclassifies it into the one set whose table a generator never writes.

⭐ The decisive property is that the generated rule is **already self-discriminating per leaf**, so widening its population is safe in a way widening the hand-authored one would not be. `collectFilledFromHashes` records a leaf only when

```
value === currentSource   ||   previous[path] === hash(value)
```

A leaf someone actually translated satisfies neither and gets **no record at all** — it stays legacy-trusted. The section list is the only part of the mechanism that cannot tell a fill from a translation; the value test can, exactly, per leaf. That is why the fix belongs in the population and not in a new predicate.

⛔ **Not the card's literal option A.** Adding `'apps'` to the `GENERATED_SECTIONS` constant would make `collectSourceLeaves` and `collectGeneratedLeaves` walk the same section, putting two predicates on one path permanently — the "two owners on one fact" the module explicitly refuses — and would assert that `apps` is *always* generated, which is false for all nine bundle sets as they ship today. The population has to follow the **run**, not the constant.

## 2. What happens to entries a human already put in `LOCALE.source-hashes.ts`

Measured, not asserted: that file holds **129 entries per locale** in `platform-objects` (100 `apps`, 20 `dashboards`, 9 `pages`), across `zh-CN` / `ja-JP` / `es-ES` — 387 human-recorded digests.

Under the proposed shape **none of them is read, written, shadowed or lost**:

- The hand table stays the sole input to `findStaleLeaves`, and `apps` stays in `HAND_AUTHORED_SECTIONS`. Nothing removes a section from the hand-authored walk.
- `collectSourceHashes` — the helper the file's own header tells a translator to use to refresh a digest — walks `HAND_AUTHORED_SECTIONS`. Unchanged.
- The extractor never writes `LOCALE.source-hashes.ts`; it writes only `LOCALE.source-hashes.generated.ts`. Two files, two tables, no merge.
- A human-translated `apps` leaf cannot acquire a generated record, because its bytes are not a copy of any recorded revision (the value test above). The overlap set is exactly the leaves a human deliberately left equal to the English source; for those, both predicates fire and both substitute the *same* source string, so the served bytes are identical either way.

⭐ The one residual cost is **discoverability, not correctness**: after the fix a path could in principle appear in both tables, and the hand file's header instructs humans to maintain a digest there. Whoever lands the population change owes that header one sentence saying which file wins for a leaf the generator also records. Naming it here so it is not discovered later.

## 3. #16242's harm claim, read at its source

**This card replaces #16242's mechanism and confirms its harm.**

#16242 attributed the missing record to the CLI's committed-section list (the literals `'objects'` / `'metadataForms'` fed to `narrowToCommittedSections`). That mechanism was falsified during its own delivery and the falsification re-measured by the dispatching seat: an `apps.*` record never enters the table, so no narrowing step can filter it out — the unnarrowed table held 775 records (2 `objects.*` + 773 `metadataForms.*`) with `apps.kpi.label` absent. The asymmetry worth recording is that **#16242's fix was still right and still landed** (both literals are gone, replaced by `translationModuleSections(bundle, kind)`), while the harm it described survived it untouched, one layer up: the CLI now commits `apps` correctly and the *population* still excludes it.

⇒ Reproduced in this PR's pin: the committed-section set contains `apps`, `GENERATED_SECTIONS` does not, and every leaf in the difference is judged by nobody.

## 4. The armed reproduction — the bytes

Driven through the real `extractTranslations` under `--no-objects-only --fill=default --source-hashes`. Fixture: one object with one field, one app `kpi`, locale `zh-CN`.

**Run 1 — the fill.** Both leaves arrive as byte copies of the `en` source:

```
bundle apps.kpi.label    = "Key Performance Indicators"
bundle objects…name.help = "The metric this KPI tracks."
provenance table         = 782 records
  record for objects.kpi_metric.fields.name.help = bbfc4790b4940413
  record for apps.kpi.label                      = (ABSENT)   <<< the gap
  sections present in table = ["objects","metadataForms"]
```

**Run 2 — the source label is revised** to `"KPI Cockpit"`; merge keeps the existing fill:

```
served apps.kpi.label    = "Key Performance Indicators"   (drifted)
current en source        = "KPI Cockpit"
record for apps.kpi.label = (ABSENT)   <<< nothing on disk records it

findStaleFills  reports  : []
findStaleLeaves reports  : []
withSourceFallback serves= "Key Performance Indicators"    <<< superseded draft
```

**The counterfactual that localizes the defect** — the same leaf, fed to the same rule under a section name the rule walks:

```
collectFilledFromHashes({objects: bundle.apps}, {objects: en.apps}, undefined)
  => { "objects.kpi.label": "becee58b40be5788" }
```

⇒ The **rule** would have recorded it. Only the **population** excludes it. (⛔ Re-rooting is not a proposed fix — it corrupts the dotted path a record is keyed by; it is here only as the discriminating measurement.)

"The same reading after the fix" is the one acceptance item this PR cannot show, for the reason in section 6.

## 5. The default `--objects-only` path is unchanged, with an ablation leg

All nine `--source-hashes` configs run under the default `--objects-only` (`objects-only` is `default: true`; `pnpm i18n:extract` passes no override), and every section the default path commits — `objects`, `metadataForms` — is already inside the population. The pin asserts that directly.

**Ablation, to prove the pin can actually fail.** `packages/cli` does not alias `@objectstack/platform-objects` (it is a `KNOWN_UNALIASED_TEST_IMPORTS` entry), so these tests resolve it through `exports` to its **`dist`** — the mutation therefore had to reach the built artifact, and was proven there rather than assumed:

| leg | on-disk proof | `dist` preflight | result |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| mutate `GENERATED_SECTIONS` to include `'apps'` | anchor count 1 → 0, replacement 0 → 1; blob differs from HEAD | `✓ marker present in 10 built files` | **3 failed / 3 passed** |
| restore + rebuild | `git diff HEAD` empty; blob byte-identical to the HEAD blob | `✓ marker absent from all 66 built files` | **6 passed**, whole-tree `git status --porcelain` empty |

The three that redden are exactly the three that encode the gap:

```
expected [ 'objects', 'metadataForms', 'apps' ] to deeply equal [ 'objects', 'metadataForms' ]
expected 'becee58b40be5788' to be undefined
expected [ 'apps.kpi.label' ] to not include 'apps.kpi.label'
```

⚠️ The first preflight attempt reported the marker ABSENT because the marker was spelled with single quotes while the build emits double quotes — recorded because it is the trap the preflight exists to catch, and the reading was redone rather than trusted.

## 6. ⛔ Why the population change is NOT in this diff

The population lives in `packages/platform-objects/src/apps/translations/source-hash.ts` — `GENERATED_SECTIONS`, `collectGeneratedLeaves`, and the signature of `collectFilledFromHashes`, which takes no section argument. That package is `domain:engine`; this card is dispatched to `domain:cli`, and editing it makes this a cross-domain PR that needs triage's designation of the file face. So it is declared and stopped at, not quietly widened into.

There is no legitimate `packages/cli`-side delivery, and the reason is a contract this file already states about itself:

> Computed by `collectFilledFromHashes` in `@objectstack/platform-objects/apps` … the extractor supplies the tree and the previous records and **owns none of the rule**.

Any CLI-side route means the extractor re-deriving the population — either reimplementing the per-leaf value test, or passing a re-rooted tree that lies about section identity and corrupts the record keys. Both make the CLI an owner of the rule. Contract-first says fix it at the producer.

⇒ What this PR leaves for the follow-up: one parameter, and the caller that fills it.

## Acceptance notes

- `noted, not filed:` #16242's body and this card both describe "the repo's one `--source-hashes` config". Nine configs use the flag today (#12559 rolled it out to all nine sets); eight pass `--objects-only` explicitly and `platform-objects` inherits the default. The dormancy conclusion is unaffected — every one of the nine is on the default path — but the count in both card bodies is stale.承接者: whoever lands the population change, whose blast-radius argument rests on that same set.
- `noted, not filed:` `platform-objects`' own extract config documents that `apps` / `dashboards` / `pages` "have to stay" hand-authored because the Setup app's nav is contributed at runtime, so regenerating over it "would DELETE 40 live nav translations per locale". ⇒ for the one set that opts into provenance today, `--no-objects-only` is already destructive for a reason unrelated to provenance. Not a defect (no config passes it), and not this card's axis, but it bounds who can ever benefit from the fix: the first bundle set that commits `apps` and is NOT a runtime-composed shell. 承接者: the population-change PR.
